title: The Black Box… Is Actually Orange! ✈️
description: An airplane's black box isn't black, and it survives incredible fire and impact! Meet the two recorders that capture everything on board.

scenes.say: An airplane's black box is actually bright orange, so it's easy to find. So what exactly does it do?
It's really two devices: one records flight data like speed, altitude and the pilot's controls, and the other records every sound in the cockpit.

scenes.label: Built to survive fire and huge impacts
scenes.say: It's built to survive eleven hundred degrees Celsius for a full hour, plus enormous impacts and pressure.

scenes.caption: Usually in the tail
scenes.say: It's usually mounted in the tail, because that's often the part most likely to survive.

scenes.text: Underwater it pings for at least 30 days
scenes.say: If it lands in the sea, it starts sending an underwater signal for at least thirty days, and newer ones for ninety days, so searchers can find it.
